content.prompt: Identify the corresponding sides and write a similarity statement.

spec.description: Unfilled, similarly oriented right triangles with all printed labels and angle givens. Coordinates establish appearance only and are not additional measurements.
spec.mathematics: A corresponds to R, B to P and C to Q. Right angles occur at A and R; angles C and Q are 40 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertex labels, right-angle marks and 40-degree givens are visible.

answer.worked:
The right angles match $A$ with $R$, and the $40^\circ$ angles match $C$ with $Q$, so $B$ matches $P$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=\angle RPQ\\\angle BCA&=\angle PQR\end{aligned}$$
Corresponding sides are $BC$ and $PQ$, $AC$ and $RQ$, and $AB$ and $RP$.
$$ABC\sim RPQ$$

spec.description: Two unfilled similar pentagons with clipped upper-left corners, larger above smaller. No numerical dimensions are asserted.
spec.mathematics: Corresponding vertices are A/L, B/M, C/N, D/P and E/Q.
spec.answerVisibility: Vertex labels only.

answer.short: $CD\sim NP$, $AE\sim LQ$; $\angle BCD=\angle MNP$, $\angle CDE=\angle NPQ$, $\angle AED=\angle LQP$, $\angle EAB=\angle QLM$; $ABCDE\sim LMNPQ$.
answer.worked:
The corresponding vertices are $A\leftrightarrow L$, $B\leftrightarrow M$, $C\leftrightarrow N$, $D\leftrightarrow P$ and $E\leftrightarrow Q$.
Corresponding sides: $AB\sim LM$, $BC\sim MN$, $CD\sim NP$, $ED\sim QP$, $AE\sim LQ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=\angle LMN\\\angle BCD&=\angle MNP\\\angle CDE&=\angle NPQ\\\angle AED&=\angle LQP\\\angle EAB&=\angle QLM\end{aligned}$$
$$ABCDE\sim LMNPQ$$

spec.description: Unfilled inverted DEF and upright JKL; coordinates derive triangles with the printed 80, 60 and 40 degree angles. All six numerical angle labels and arcs remain.
spec.mathematics: D/L are 80 degrees, E/K are 60 degrees and F/J are 40 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: All vertex and angle givens remain visible; no response answers are drawn.

answer.short: $DE\sim LK$, $EF\sim KJ$, $FD\sim JL$; $\angle EFD=\angle KJL$, $\angle FDE=\angle JLK$; $DEF\sim LKJ$.
answer.worked:
Match the equal angles: $D\leftrightarrow L$ ($80^\circ$), $E\leftrightarrow K$ ($60^\circ$), $F\leftrightarrow J$ ($40^\circ$).
Corresponding sides: $DE\sim LK$, $EF\sim KJ$, $FD\sim JL$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle DEF&=\angle LKJ\\\angle EFD&=\angle KJL\\\angle FDE&=\angle JLK\end{aligned}$$
$$DEF\sim LKJ$$

spec.description: Unfilled similar triangles in the source orientations. Matching single arcs at N/T and double arcs at P/U determine correspondence; no numerical angles or lengths are introduced.
spec.mathematics: M corresponds to V, N to T and P to U.
spec.answerVisibility: Only vertex labels and supplied matching angle arcs are visible.

answer.short: $MP\sim VU$, $PN\sim UT$, $NM\sim TV$; $\angle MPN=\angle VUT$, $\angle PNM=\angle UTV$, $\angle NMP=\angle TVU$; $MPN\sim VUT$.
answer.worked:
The double arcs match $P$ with $U$, and the single arcs match $N$ with $T$, so $M$ matches $V$.
Corresponding sides: $MP\sim VU$, $PN\sim UT$, $NM\sim TV$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle MPN&=\angle VUT\\\angle PNM&=\angle UTV\\\angle NMP&=\angle TVU\end{aligned}$$
$$MPN\sim VUT$$

spec.description: Oppositely oriented similar right triangles; the second is larger. Matching filled dots identify B and H.
spec.mathematics: A corresponds to G, B to H and C to I. Right angles at A and G.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and markers; no answers.

answer.short: $AB\sim GH$, $BC\sim HI$, $CA\sim IG$; $\angle CAB=\angle IGH$, $\angle ABC=\angle GHI$, $\angle BCA=\angle HIG$; $ABC\sim GHI$.
answer.worked:
The right-angle markers match $A$ with $G$, and the dots match $B$ with $H$. Therefore $C$ matches $I$.
$$\begin{aligned}AB&\sim GH\\BC&\sim HI\\CA&\sim IG\\\angle CAB&=\angle IGH\\\angle ABC&=\angle GHI\\\angle BCA&=\angle HIG\end{aligned}$$
Thus $ABC\sim GHI$.

spec.description: Reflected similar triangles; matching dots at A and M and matching crosses at C and O. The second triangle is larger.
spec.mathematics: A corresponds to M, B to N and C to O.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and markers; no answers.

answer.short: $AB\sim MN$, $BC\sim NO$, $CA\sim OM$; $\angle ACB=\angle MON$, $\angle CAB=\angle OMN$, $\angle CBA=\angle ONM$; $ABC\sim MNO$.
answer.worked:
The dots match $A$ with $M$, and the crosses match $C$ with $O$. Therefore $B$ matches $N$.
$$\begin{aligned}AB&\sim MN\\BC&\sim NO\\CA&\sim OM\\\angle ACB&=\angle MON\\\angle CAB&=\angle OMN\\\angle CBA&=\angle ONM\end{aligned}$$
Thus $ABC\sim MNO$.

answer.short: $AD\sim AB$, $DE\sim BC$, $EA\sim CA$; $\angle ADE=\angle ABC$, $\angle DEA=\angle BCA$, $\angle EAD=\angle CAB$; $ADE\sim ABC$.
answer.worked:
Consider triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$. The dots match $D$ with $B$. The angles at $A$ are vertically opposite; $ED\parallel BC$ matches $E$ with $C$.
$$\begin{aligned}AD&\sim AB\\DE&\sim BC\\EA&\sim CA\\\angle ADE&=\angle ABC\\\angle DEA&=\angle BCA\\\angle EAD&=\angle CAB\end{aligned}$$
Thus $ADE\sim ABC$.

spec.description: Nested triangles ABE and ACD share A. BE and CD have matching upward parallel arrows.
spec.mathematics: A,B,C are collinear; A,E,D are collinear; BE is parallel to CD. A corresponds to A, B to C and E to D.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and markers; no answers.

inlines.text: (Hint: Redraw the diagram as two triangles)

answer.short: $AB\sim AC$, $AE\sim AD$, $EB\sim DC$; $\angle EAB=\angle DAC$, $\angle EBA=\angle DCA$, $\angle AEB=\angle ADC$; $ABE\sim ACD$.
answer.worked:
Consider triangles $ABE$ and $ACD$. They share the angle at $A$. Since $BE\parallel CD$, corresponding angles match $B$ with $C$ and $E$ with $D$.
$$\begin{aligned}AB&\sim AC\\AE&\sim AD\\EB&\sim DC\\\angle EAB&=\angle DAC\\\angle EBA&=\angle DCA\\\angle AEB&=\angle ADC\end{aligned}$$
Thus $ABE\sim ACD$.

content.prompt:
Here are two triangles, X and Y.

Explain why triangle X is not similar to triangle Y.

spec.description: Two unshaded triangles on a shared 10-column, 6-row square grid, preserving the common baseline, equal heights and differing base widths. The mathematical triangle outlines prevent use of a blank-grid template.
spec.mathematics: Measured from the lower-left grid corner: X has vertices (1,1), (3,1), (2,5); Y has vertices (5,1), (9,1), (7,5). Bases are 2 and 4 grid units; both heights are 4 grid units.
spec.answerVisibility: The triangle labels and grid are givens; measurements and explanations appear only in answers.

answer.short: Y has twice the base of X but the same height, so the triangles are not similar.
answer.worked:
X has base $2$ grid units and height $4$ grid units. Y has base $4$ grid units and height $4$ grid units.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Base ratio}&=\frac{4}{2}=2\\\text{Height ratio}&=\frac{4}{4}=1\end{align*}$$
The ratios differ, so Y is not a uniform enlargement of X.

answer.worked:
$CE$ corresponds to $BC$ and $DE$ corresponds to $AB$.

content.prompt:
In the diagram below, triangle $ACE$ is similar to triangle $BCD$.

If $AB=x$, $BC=5$, $CD=4x$ and $DE=2$, find the value of $x$. Leave your answer as a surd.

spec.meaningfulRelationships: B lies on AC, D lies on EC, and AE and BD are parallel. Segment labels distinguish the whole corresponding sides from their constituent lengths.

answer.short:
$x=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{2}$.

Use $AC=x+5$ and $EC=2+4x$ in the corresponding-side proportion, then take the positive root.
answer.worked:
From $\triangle ACE\sim\triangle BCD$, $AC$ corresponds to $BC$ and $EC$ corresponds to $DC$. The whole lengths are $AC=x+5$ and $EC=2+4x$.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x+5}{5}&=\frac{2+4x}{4x}\\4x(x+5)&=5(2+4x)\\4x^2+20x&=10+20x\\4x^2&=10.\end{aligned}$$

Since $x$ is a positive length, $x=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{2}$.

spec.meaningfulRelationships: Preserves the worked diagram's solved subdivision 5/(5+x), parallel sides and the four segment labels.

content.prompt:
Two similar right-angled triangles are shown.

The length of side $AB$ is $8\text{ cm}$ and the length of side $EF$ is $4\text{ cm}$. The area of triangle $ABC$ is $20\text{ cm}^2$.

Calculate the length in centimetres of side $DF$ in Triangle II, correct to two decimal places.

spec.meaningfulRelationships: Horizontal bases AB and DE, vertical legs BC and EF, right-angle marks at B and E, and matching angle dots at A and D. DF is the second hypotenuse.

answer.short:
$7.55\text{ cm}$.

Use the area to find $BC$, scale $AB$ to find $DE$, then apply Pythagoras' theorem in Triangle II.
answer.worked: Using the area of Triangle I, $20=\tfrac12\times8\times BC$, so $BC=5\text{ cm}$. The scale factor from Triangle I to Triangle II is $EF/BC=4/5$. Therefore $DE=8\times\tfrac45=6.4\text{ cm}$. By Pythagoras' theorem, $DF=\sqrt{6.4^2+4^2}=\sqrt{56.96}\text{ cm}$, which rounds to $7.55\text{ cm}$.

content.prompt:
In the diagram below, $IJKH$ and $IHML$ are similar figures.

$IJ=4\text{ cm}$

$HM=16\text{ cm}$

Diagram is not to scale.

Find the scale factor of $IJKH$ to $IHML$.

spec.meaningfulRelationships: The smaller rectangle is the left part of the larger rectangle. The side IH is shared and the given correspondence matches IJ with IH and IH with HM. The 16 cm dimension spans the entire large rectangle.
spec.calibration: Retained the source TikZ coordinate ratios and provided a native bounding box. Check label spacing and physical type size in print.

answer.short:
$2$

Use the shared side $IH$ in the proportion $IJ/IH=IH/HM$.
answer.worked: Let $IH=x\text{ cm}$. The similarity in the given vertex order gives $\dfrac{IJ}{IH}=\dfrac{IH}{HM}$. Hence $\dfrac4x=\dfrac{x}{16}$ and $x^2=64$. Since $x$ is a positive length, $x=8$. The scale factor from $IJKH$ to $IHML$ is $\dfrac{IH}{IJ}=\dfrac84=2$.

entries.description:
Scale Factor
• Similar figures have corresponding sides in the same ratio.
• This ratio is called the scale factor, k.
• The scale factor is the number you multiply the original shape by to get the image.

entries.description:

Reduction: k < 1; the image is smaller than the original.
Congruent: k = 1; the image is identical, or congruent, to the original.
Enlargement: k > 1; the image is larger than the original.

entries.description: Finding Lengths in Scale Drawings

Scale Drawings
A scale drawing is a smaller or larger drawing of a real-life object.
Examples include maps, house plans, and scientific diagrams.
We call the real-life object the original, and the drawing the image.
Scales for scale drawings are written in simplified ratio notation:

image : original
1 : n
